newsitem.title: USA: Apparent suicides heartbreaking, shocking - Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Apparent suicides heartbreaking, shocking - Clinton.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Thursday he was shocked and sickened by the apparent mass suicide of 39 men and women in California.

"It's heartbreaking, sickening...shocking," Clinton said when asked his reaction to the mass deaths in Rancho Santa Fe, California. He said he did not know any more about the incident than he had seen in media reports.
"It's very troubling to me but I don't think I know enough to make a definitive comment about it," a sombre Clinton added during a White House photo session on health care.

"It's important that we get as many facts as we can about this and try to determine what in fact motivated those people and what all of us can do to make sure that there aren't other people thinking in that same way out there in our country and that aren't so isolated that they can create a world for themselves that may justifiy that kind of thing," he said.
The bodies of 39 men and women, cloaked in purple shrouds, were found in a million-dollar California mansion in what police said appeared to be a mass suicide.

Cmdr. Alan Fulmer of the San Diego County Sheriff's Department told a news conference the cause of death remained a mystery but said he believed the 39 took their lives in a ritual that left them appearing as though they had died peacefully in their sleep.
